subject: religious-studies
topicDisplay: Islam: Rites of Passage & Family Life
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On which day after a child's birth is the Aqiqah ceremony traditionally performed?
questions.explain: The Aqiqah, including naming and shaving of the head, is traditionally carried out on the seventh day after birth.

questions.q: What is whispered into the right ear of a newborn Muslim baby shortly after birth?
questions.explain: The Adhan is whispered into the baby's right ear so that the first words it hears relate to God.

questions.q: During Aqiqah, the baby's head is shaved and a donation to charity is given equal to the weight of the hair in which material?
questions.explain: The weight of the shaved hair is calculated in silver (or gold) and an equivalent value is given to charity.

questions.q: What is the name of the practice of rubbing a small piece of softened date onto a newborn's gums or palate?
questions.explain: Tahnik is the Sunnah practice of placing a little softened date in the newborn's mouth.

questions.q: What is the Islamic marriage contract or ceremony called?
questions.explain: The Nikah is the marriage contract that forms the legal and religious basis of a Muslim marriage.

questions.q: What is the term for the gift or dowry given by the groom to the bride in a Muslim marriage?
questions.explain: The Mahr is the dowry given by the groom to the bride, which becomes her own property.

questions.q: The wedding feast held to celebrate a marriage and announce it publicly is known as the:
questions.explain: The Walimah is the marriage feast, a Sunnah that publicly announces and celebrates the union.

questions.q: What is the special congregational prayer performed at a Muslim funeral called?
questions.explain: Salat al-Janazah is the funeral prayer offered by the community for the deceased.

questions.q: The plain white cloth in which a Muslim body is wrapped for burial is called the:
questions.explain: The kafan is the simple white shroud used to wrap the washed body before burial.

questions.q: Why is the Adhan whispered into a newborn's ear rather than any other words?
options: To protect the baby from illness through magic
So the first sounds the child hears affirm belief in one God
Because it is required for the child to inherit property
To announce the baby's name to relatives
questions.explain: Beginning life with the words of the Adhan symbolises that the child is welcomed into the faith of Islam.

questions.q: What does the giving of charity equal to the weight of the baby's hair best demonstrate about Islamic birth rites?
options: That wealth must be hidden from the poor
That generosity and gratitude to God accompany the celebration of new life
That the baby must repay a debt
That only rich families may perform Aqiqah
questions.explain: Linking the new birth to charity expresses thankfulness to God and concern for those in need.

questions.q: Why is the giving of the Mahr significant for the bride in a Muslim marriage?
options: It is paid to the bride's father as a fee
It gives the bride financial security and independence as her own property
It must be returned to the groom after the wedding
It replaces the need for a marriage contract
questions.explain: The Mahr belongs solely to the bride, providing her with security and recognising her rights.

questions.q: Muslims regard marriage primarily as which of the following?
options: A purely private matter needing no witnesses
A sacred and social contract encouraged by the Prophet Muhammad
A ceremony that cannot be ended under any circumstances
An optional practice discouraged in Islam
questions.explain: Marriage in Islam is a contract and a Sunnah, seen as the proper basis for family life.

questions.q: Why are Muslim funerals kept simple, with a plain shroud and burial rather than cremation?
options: Because coffins are forbidden in all countries
To show equality in death and respect for the God-given body
Because cremation is cheaper and quicker
To allow the body to be preserved for many years
questions.explain: Simplicity reflects that all are equal before God, and burial preserves the dignity of the body.

questions.q: When a Muslim is buried, the body is placed in the grave so that it faces which direction?
questions.explain: The body is laid on its right side facing Makkah, the same direction Muslims face in prayer.

questions.q: According to the Qur'an, how should Muslim children treat their parents, especially in old age?
options: With indifference once they are adults
By sending them away from the family home
Only with financial support and nothing else
questions.explain: The Qur'an commands believers to show kindness and respect to parents, particularly as they grow old.

questions.q: Why is the family considered so important within Islam?
options: Because it replaces the need for daily prayer
Because it is the basis of a stable society and where faith is taught to children
Because families are required to live entirely apart from society
Because only married people may enter the mosque
questions.explain: The family nurtures the next generation in faith and forms the foundation of the wider Muslim community.

questions.q: A Muslim couple celebrate the birth of their baby boy and follow the Sunnah tradition of Aqiqah. How many animals are traditionally sacrificed for a boy?
questions.explain: Tradition recommends two sheep or goats for a boy and one for a girl, the meat shared including with the poor.

questions.q: A family is arranging the funeral of a relative who has just died. In line with Islamic teaching, what should they do first with the body?
options: Embalm and display it for a week
Perform ghusl, the ritual washing of the body
Dress the body in the deceased's finest clothes
questions.explain: The body is first washed (ghusl), then wrapped in the kafan before the funeral prayer and prompt burial.

questions.q: A young Muslim wants to honour their religious duties within family life. Which action best reflects Islamic teaching on the family?
options: Ignoring elderly grandparents to focus on personal goals
Caring for elderly parents and maintaining strong family ties
Refusing to help with any household responsibilities
questions.explain: Islam places great emphasis on caring for parents and preserving bonds of kinship within the family.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Islam: Rites of Passage & Family Life
